title: Canary pacing, observability contract, and ops SLA for experiment ramps
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Purpose: define a repeatable, metrics-driven contract for canary ramps and A/B experiments that ties pacing to observability signals, cost limits, and quality regressions. This ticket creates the canonical checklist and SLOs that PMs, Eng, and SREs use to approve staged traffic increases and automatic transitions between canary -> ramp -> full rollout. Scope: Redwood-hosted and Dedicated routing paths; experiments that touch model selection, routing policy changes (region/cost-based), batching/cache behavior, and runtime kernel/config changes. Excludes enterprise-only private deployments that require separate compliance sign-off.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A published observability contract document lives in Confluence and is linked from this ticket. 2) Monitoring and alerts for canary SLOs are implemented in Datadog/Prometheus and validated against a synthetic traffic job. 3) Automated pacing rules (percent traffic schedule + pause conditions) are encoded in rollout config and tested in staging. 4) A runbook for on-call actions and automatic rollback is reviewed and approved by SRE. 5) A small pilot experiment (5% -> 20% -> 50%) completes without triggering critical alerts under normal noise for 2 weeks.
milestones: Pacing automation added to rollout engine + unit tests (2025-03-10)
Staging pilot run and blameless review (2025-03-21)
metrics: Latency: p50/p95/p99 token-gen latency delta vs baseline (target: p95 increase <10% absolute and <200ms)
Error rate: client-visible 4xx/5xx and model-side decode errors (target: no >0.05% absolute increase)
Quality: eval set BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim delta and user-rated quality sample (target: no regression >1.5% on primary eval metric)
Cost: cost-per-1k-tokens delta (target: increase <=15% for canary tier)
Throughput: successful requests/sec and queue depth under identical synthetic load
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): 2% traffic for 48-72h. Enable full observability and synthetic canary traffic. Phase 2 (Ramp): increase to 10% for 72h if no threshold breaches. Phase 3 (Broader ramp): 25% for 48h, then 50% for 24h. Final: full rollout only after passing automated acceptance checks and exec sign-off. Each phase has pause conditions: critical SLO breach, untriaged errors, or quality regression on sampled prompt set.
rollback_criteria: Immediate rollback to previous model/route version if any of: 1) p95 latency increase >300ms absolute or >25% relative for more than 15m. 2) client-visible error rate spike >0.25% absolute sustained for 10m. 3) Quality regression >3% on the gated eval set or >=5% drop in human-rated sample. 4) Cost blowouts >50% baseline for sustained 1h. Rollback must trigger an incident in PagerDuty and a postmortem within 72h.
open_questions: Do we require SRE approval for experiments that only change batching/kv-cache parameters?
What is the canonical small eval prompt set we should use for live quality gating (who owns it)?
Should Dedicated customers have separate pacing thresholds by default?
Do we need an opt-in for customers to be routed to canary variants in hosted API?
